name: The Dragon Oak of Lozorno

location.address: Forest on the Kopanicka hill above Lozorno village, reached via a marked cycling/hiking trail (the former forest railway route toward Kosarisko), Malacky District, Bratislava Region, Slovakia
location.neighbourhood: Kopanicka hill, Male Karpaty Protected Landscape Area, above Lozorno

access: Free, in public forest inside the Male Karpaty Protected Landscape Area. Reached via a signed cycling/hiking trail from Lozorno village (park near the village water reservoir, continue east on the asphalt forest road). No gate, ticket or private-land concern in any source.
transport: STANDALONE PLACE, not a Bratislava day trip: the tree stands in forest above Lozorno village, reached only by the marked trail; the nearest Bratislava bus connection (line 269, Lozorno to Bratislava Autobusova stanica) runs about 44 minutes plus the forest walk/ride from the village, past the roughly 30-minute day-trip boundary. Treat Lozorno as its own place under the single-famous-tree exception (2026-08-31): would somebody travel specifically for this one tree? Yes: 2022 Slovak national Tree of the Year, then silver medal (2nd of 17) at the 2023 European Tree of the Year with 18,198 votes, beaten only by Poland's Oak Fabrykant.
story:
In 2023 only one tree in Europe drew more votes than this oak: Poland's Oak Fabrykant. The Dragon Oak of Lozorno took silver at the European Tree of the Year, second of seventeen with 18,198 votes, a year after winning Slovakia's national title. It is named for the way it looks, a silhouette Slovak writers compare to a dragon sitting down, with deeply scarred and gnarled bark.

The trunk is nearly seven metres round, 677 centimetres by one report. Experts put it at around 700 years, an estimate rather than a ring count, so the honest band is 600 to 800. Its height depends on who you read: 18 metres in one account, 24 in another.

The sources tie its long life to the building of nearby Pajštún Castle, to the Croatian merchants who later settled around Lozorno, and to a forest railway since abandoned. That railway's route is now the cycling and hiking trail that leads to it: park by the village reservoir and follow the asphalt forest road east into the Malé Karpaty hills. Deer move through here, including rare white fallow deer, and beavers have come back to the nearby Suchý creek.

The worry is timber. The contest page and other coverage from 2023 name logging in the surrounding forest as a threat. That coverage is the most recent we have found; if you have walked up since, tell us how it looks. The pin is approximate, so watch for the trail signs.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by the trunk, nearly 7 metres round, and the dragon-like silhouette with deeply scarred, gnarled bark. It stands in forest on Kopanicka hill, along the marked trail from Lozorno.
